hits.name: Codie Sanchez
hits.hook: "Buying a small business is like buying yourself a second job."  How a few of those “jobs” are doing
hits.text:
"Buying a small business is like buying yourself a second job."

How a few of those “jobs” are doing:

→ Warren Buffett: bought control of a dying New England textile mill called Berkshire Hathaway in 1965 and turned it into a conglomerate worth over $1 trillion.

→ Howard Schultz: bought a Seattle coffee bean company with 6 stores for $3.8M in 1987. Today Starbucks has over 41,000 stores doing $37B a year.

→ Les Schwab: sold his house and borrowed $11k to buy a tire shop when he was still a newspaper circulation manager. Today it's 600+ stores doing over a billion in sales.

→ Carl Karcher: borrowed against his car to buy a hot dog cart while working his job. By 1943 he had 4 hot dog locations. Today Carl's Jr. has about 1,000 restaurants around the US.

→ Wayne Huizenga: borrowed $5k from his dad to buy a used garbage truck and a few customers. That became Waste Management, now a $25B/year company.

→ Kenn Ricci: bought a small charter company for $27.5k and grew it into the aviation group that bought Flexjet, now flying 340+ jets.

Sure, you can buy yourself a job. Also they aren’t always bad.

Or you can buy a business with enough profit to pay an operator, then grow it, increase its value, and exit. Those take more looking, but they exist.

I bought my first business with less than $100k while working 60-70 hour weeks in finance.

I've seen hundreds of people in our Academy do the same, even while working their W2s.

Every name on this list started by buying something small.
